concepts.name: MPI: Conceptual Foundation and the Capability Approach
key_dimensions: Amartya Sen's capability approach as the philosophical basis vs. income-based poverty measures
Distinction between 'deprivation' in MPI vs. 'poverty line' in monetary measures
Why MPI captures 'texture of poverty' beyond income thresholds
UPSC trap: MPI measures poverty, NOT inequality — confusion with Gini coefficient

concepts.name: Global MPI: Institutional Architecture and Custodians
key_dimensions: Jointly developed by UNDP and Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI) — not UNDP alone
Released as part of Human Development Report (HDR) but is a separate index
OPHI's role vs. UNDP's role: methodology vs. publication
UPSC trap: MPI is NOT a World Bank index; confusion with $2.15/day poverty line

concepts.name: Three Dimensions of Global MPI: Health, Education, Living Standards
key_dimensions: Exact three dimensions: Health, Education, Living Standards (not 'income' as a dimension)
Why 'income' is deliberately excluded as a direct dimension
Overlap and distinctions with Human Development Index (HDI) dimensions
UPSC trap: HDI has 'income' dimension; MPI replaces it with 'Living Standards'

concepts.name: Ten Indicators of Global MPI and Their Weightage
key_dimensions: Health (2 indicators): Nutrition, Child mortality — each weighted 1/6
Education (2 indicators): Years of schooling, School attendance — each weighted 1/6
Living Standards (6 indicators): Cooking fuel, Sanitation, Drinking water, Electricity, Housing, Assets — each weighted 1/18
UPSC trap: Unequal sub-weights within dimensions; Living Standards has 6 indicators but same total weight as Health/Education

concepts.name: Dual Cutoff Method (Alkire-Foster Method)
key_dimensions: First cutoff: Deprivation cutoff — whether a household is deprived in each indicator
Second cutoff: Poverty cutoff — a person is MPI-poor if deprived in 33.3% or more weighted indicators
Why dual cutoff avoids 'aggregation problem' of single-dimensional measures
UPSC trap: A person deprived in only 1-2 indicators is NOT counted as MPI-poor; 33.3% threshold is critical

concepts.name: MPI Score Computation: Incidence (H) and Intensity (A)
key_dimensions: Incidence (H): Headcount ratio — share of population that is MPI-poor
Intensity (A): Average share of weighted deprivations among the poor
MPI = H × A; this product form is the key formula
UPSC trap: Two countries can have same MPI but different H and A — policy implications differ

concepts.name: Vulnerability and Severe Poverty Sub-categories within MPI
key_dimensions: Vulnerable to poverty: Deprived in 20–33.3% of weighted indicators
Severely poor: Deprived in 50% or more of weighted indicators
Near-poor vs. severely poor distinction and policy targeting implications
UPSC trap: 'Vulnerable' category does NOT count in MPI score computation

concepts.name: India's National MPI (NITI Aayog) vs. Global MPI
key_dimensions: India's National MPI released by NITI Aayog using NFHS data — not the global MPI methodology exactly
National MPI uses 12 indicators across same 3 dimensions (expanded from 10 global indicators)
Additional indicators in National MPI: Maternal health, Bank account, Assets (modified)
UPSC trap: National MPI and Global MPI use different indicator sets — India's ranking differs depending on which is used

concepts.name: Data Sources for India's MPI Computation
key_dimensions: Global MPI for India primarily uses National Family Health Survey (NFHS) data
NITI Aayog uses NFHS-5 (2019-21) for national MPI baseline
DHS (Demographic and Health Survey) as the international standard data source for most countries
UPSC trap: Census data is NOT used for MPI computation; NFHS is the primary source

concepts.name: India's Performance in Global MPI: Trends and Key Statistics
key_dimensions: India lifted 415 million people out of multidimensional poverty between 2005-06 and 2019-21 (UNDP/OPHI report)
India's MPI value declined from 0.283 (2005-06) to 0.069 (2019-21) — significant improvement
Nutrition remains the largest contributor to India's MPI score
UPSC trap: India's improvement in MPI does NOT mean improvement in income inequality (Gini)

concepts.name: State-Level MPI Disparities in India
key_dimensions: Bihar, Jharkhand, UP, MP — highest MPI values (most poor states)
Kerala, Goa, Sikkim — lowest MPI values
Rural-urban MPI gap and its trend over time
UPSC trap: High GSDP states may still have high MPI in certain indicators (e.g., Gujarat: high income, high malnutrition)

concepts.name: MPI vs. Other Poverty Measures: Tendulkar, Rangarajan, and World Bank Lines
key_dimensions: Tendulkar Committee: Calorie-based poverty line (consumption expenditure proxy)
Rangarajan Committee: Revised upward; also consumption-based
World Bank: $2.15/day (2017 PPP) — monetary, unidimensional
UPSC trap: MPI multidimensional poor ≠ BPL (Below Poverty Line) list — different methodologies yield different counts

concepts.name: MPI and Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) Linkage
key_dimensions: SDG 1 (No Poverty): MPI directly tracks multidimensional poverty — but SDG 1.2 specifically references multidimensional poverty
MPI indicators map onto multiple SDGs: SDG 2 (hunger), SDG 3 (health), SDG 4 (education), SDG 6 (water), SDG 7 (energy)
MPI as a monitoring tool for SDG progress — UNDP explicitly uses it
UPSC trap: MPI tracks SDG 1.2, NOT SDG 1.1 (which uses $2.15/day monetary line)

concepts.name: Criticisms and Limitations of MPI
key_dimensions: Equal weighting assumption: Are health and education equally important as living standards?
Binary deprivation scoring: Does not capture degree of deprivation within an indicator
Data availability constraint: Relies on survey data which may be outdated or inconsistent across countries
UPSC trap: MPI cannot be used for year-on-year comparison unless survey data is updated — Indian NFHS gap was 10 years (2005-06 to 2015-16)

concepts.name: MPI and Gender: Women's Specific Deprivations
key_dimensions: MPI is household-level index — does NOT directly capture intra-household gender inequality
Gender-disaggregated MPI analysis: Women more deprived in nutrition and years of schooling indicators
OPHI's Gender and MPI research: Women-headed households vs. male-headed households
UPSC trap: MPI does NOT have a gender sub-index unlike GII (Gender Inequality Index) — different instruments

concepts.name: MPI and Social Group Disparities in India: SC/ST Analysis
key_dimensions: SC/ST populations show significantly higher MPI values than general category
Tribal districts and forest-dwelling communities face compound deprivations
NITI Aayog's MPI report explicitly disaggregates by social groups
UPSC trap: MPI improvement at national level can mask persistent SC/ST deprivation — aggregation hides group-level inequality

concepts.name: Aspirational Districts Programme (ADP) and MPI Convergence
key_dimensions: NITI Aayog identified 112 aspirational districts largely on basis of MPI-linked indicators
ADP uses 49 indicators across Health & Nutrition, Education, Agriculture, Basic Infrastructure, Financial Inclusion
MPI as a policy tool for targeted convergence of government schemes
UPSC trap: ADP indicators are NOT identical to MPI indicators — ADP is broader and includes financial inclusion

concepts.name: Human Development Index (HDI) vs. MPI: Conceptual Overlap and Differences
key_dimensions: HDI: Country-level average achievement in 3 dimensions (health, education, income)
MPI: Household-level deprivation in 3 dimensions (health, education, living standards) — identifies the poor
HDI uses GNI per capita; MPI uses no income indicator directly
UPSC trap: A country can improve HDI while MPI stagnates if gains are concentrated among non-poor

concepts.name: UNDP's 2024 MPI Report: Global Findings and India's Position
key_dimensions: 1.1 billion people live in acute multidimensional poverty globally (as per recent UNDP-OPHI reports)
South Asia and Sub-Saharan Africa account for largest share of MPI poor
India no longer in top 10 most MPI-poor countries — significant improvement noted
UPSC trap: Despite improvement in MPI rank, India still has largest absolute number of poor in some sub-indicators like nutrition

concepts.name: Cooking Fuel as MPI Indicator: Policy Implications
key_dimensions: Household deprived if cooking with dung, wood, charcoal, coal — 'dirty fuels'
Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY) directly addresses this MPI indicator
Connection between cooking fuel deprivation, women's health, and indoor air pollution (SDG 3 and SDG 7)
UPSC trap: Owning an LPG connection ≠ regular LPG use — MPI refill data shows persistent deprivation despite scheme
